meta.title: Andhericha Raja
meta.location: Ganesh Maidan, Azad Nagar II, Veera Desai Road, Andheri West, Mumbai 400053
meta.foundedNote: Institutional history and contemporary English and Marathi reporting agree on 1966; sources disagree on the start of the later-immersion tradition.
meta.intro: Andhericha Raja is the public Ganeshotsav of Azad Nagar Sarvajanik Utsav Samiti, founded in 1966 by workers settling around Andheri's industrial workplaces. Its best-known ritual distinction is the large idol's immersion on the Sankashti following Anant Chaturdashi, while a smaller puja idol follows the earlier calendar. Changing temple-inspired sets and the community's labour history both belong in this collection. The date when the later immersion began remains disputed across the available institutional and press accounts.

paragraphs.text: The mandal's history places its beginning in 1966 among workers of Golden Tobacco, Tata Special Steel and Excel Industries. It describes people moving from Lalbaug and Parel into Azad Nagar housing near Andheri workplaces. Contemporary retrospective reporting also identifies this industrial community as the festival's foundation, making work, migration and neighbourhood building central archival themes.

The institution links its wish-fulfilling reputation and later immersion to a vow during a factory strike. Such accounts document community belief rather than establish supernatural causation. The official history and Indian Express give 1975, while Sakal quotes a 1973 beginning and Mid-day refers to 1972-73. The collection preserves the disagreement instead of selecting one date by repetition.

sections.title: A ritual calendar beyond Anant Chaturdashi

paragraphs.text: The smaller puja idol is immersed on Anant Chaturdashi; the life-size display idol follows on Sankashti. The inspected 2024 press scene records the large garlanded deity on a flower-covered procession platform. A separate 2025 institutional photograph shows a much smaller idol being carried in a workshop. Keeping those objects distinct prevents a gallery label from becoming a false claim about the main idol's scale.

The 2025 programme describes a Sarangpur Kashtabhanjan Hanuman temple setting, with art direction attributed to Dharmesh Shah. Marathi reporting independently describes the set and a thirty-two-foot fibre Hanuman feature. That measurement belongs to the scenic Hanuman, not the Ganesh idol. The changing architecture and decorative trades should therefore be recorded alongside the recurring deity and immersion customs.

The official annual albums now support an inspected sequence from 2016 through 2026. They mix installed-idol views, workshop handovers, visitors and later religious events. Only frames showing Ganesh in a physical installation are used for this series. Album headings establish institutional year attribution; resemblance between recurring faces does not establish a date.

The theme archive separates the reduced pandemic installations from the surrounding years. It describes four-foot idols, local immersion ponds and online viewing for 2020-21, followed by a Lakshmi Vilas Palace setting in 2022. This gives the photographs a history of changing scale and public access, alongside the temple-inspired scenery.

years.title: Dilwara temple setting
years.summary: At Azad Nagar, the 2012 Andhericha Raja pandal took its design from the Jain Dilwara temples near Mount Abu. Preparations included a replica with 60 carved pillars, and Rediff identified the same theme during the festival.

claims.text: The festival began in 1966 among local industrial workers.
Large and small idols follow distinct immersion days.
The start year for the later immersion is unresolved.
The 2025 thirty-two-foot figure is Hanuman scenery.
The selected 2025 workshop photograph shows a small carried idol.

researchNotes.coverage: Institutional history and contact, English retrospective, contemporary 2024 procession gallery, 2025 official gallery, organiser programme and Marathi reporting. Both selected images visually inspected. Phase 2: 10 annual entries supplemented after direct image inspection; source labels and photographic appearance assessed separately.
gaps: No authenticated annual photographs before 2016 obtained.
Official albums supply year attribution but no independently authenticated capture dates or photographer identities.
The start date of the Sankashti immersion tradition remains disputed.
Smaller carried Ganesh figures and non-Ganesh religious scenes occur in the albums; their precise ritual roles require captions.
nextActions: Obtain a captioned full view of the 2025 main idol and dated making sequence.
Resolve the strike chronology with contemporary records; retain devotional language as attributed belief.
